newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Malaysia says can't back ITA plan in current form.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says can't back ITA plan in current form.

text.p: Malaysia said on Friday it could not back a U.S. plan to free global trade in information technology products by the year 2000 in its current form.
Malaysian Trade Minister Rafidah Aziz told Reuters Financial Television in an interview at the annual APEC conference here that the agreement did not offer enough flexibility.
"We cannot be in a hurry, for example to have APEC endorse (such) an agreement for signing," she said.

Washington is hoping that the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum will back the proposed Information Technology Agreement (ITA) that would eradicate tariffs on computers and related products by the year 2000.
APEC approval would give the plan a head start at the inaugural ministerial meeting next month of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), where the United States will formally submit the proposal.
Asked if she thought the WTO meeting in Singapore could endorse the ITA agreement in its current form, Rafidah said: "As it stands I doubt it very much."

She said that in order for the proposal to win the support of Malaysia, "there must be assurances that flexibilities are given to such countries that need flexibility in the area of the timeframe and in product coverage".
APEC officials and delegates said on Friday ministers from the group's 18 member economies would issue a vaguely worded statement welcoming ongoing talks on the ITA.
